View Test Case
Preconditions
Staging environment selected. Collection variables cleared.
Steps
  1. 1. POST V1 Search (api/FlightSearch/Search) with the above body. 2. POST V2 Search (api/V2/FlightSearch/Search) with the same criteria. 3. Record offers count, canBeHeld, haveBundles and offerHasAncillary per offer.
Expected Result
HTTP 200 on both versions with non-empty offers[]; no 'credentials ... do not exist or are not active' error. canBeHeld=true expected (baseline 67/67) so Hold-based cases are runnable; haveBundles=false expected so Bundle+Void flows are out of scope.
Actual Result
Both versions 200 with 53 offers (baseline 67 on 2026-08-05; the count differs with date and live inventory). canBeHeld 53/53 so every Hold-based case is runnable; haveBundles 0/53 so Bundle+Void flows stay out of scope. V2 offerHasAncillary is true on 25 offers (SPEC 4.6 Ancillary is Conditional); no ANC/SM + Void flow is in this file. The first V1 Search of the session took 65.8s (V2 3.0s), the same cold-start delay seen in Round 1.

Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 passed. Staging only.
Steps
  1. 1. V1: Search -> FareConfirm -> Book. V2: Search -> FareConfirm -> AddPassenger -> Book. 2. Record pnr, gdsPNR, bookingToken, tickets[] (ticketNumber, ticketStatus, carrierCode), ticketingDate, voidCapability.
Expected Result
HTTP 200; pnr, gdsPNR, bookingToken non-empty; tickets[] populated with ticketStatus=Booked (baseline 2026-08-05: Book issued QR tickets synchronously in ~28s). Record whether voidCapability is now present and its exact enum value as the 'void allowed' baseline; if absent, log it as a recurrence of the missing-voidCapability defect (absent on TravelportNdc 2026-08-05, on SabreNdc 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-25).
Actual Result
Both Book calls are synchronous: pnr, gdsPNR and bookingToken are present and tickets[] holds one Booked ticket (baseline matched, ~22s). voidCapability is now returned on Book and Retrieve with the value FullVoidOnlyAllowed, which is the recorded "void allowed" baseline (it was absent in Round 1 and on 2026-08-05). One new anomaly: the V1 booking 774MNY and the V2 booking 773JKY, made in the same second, were given the identical bookingToken 96e14dee-43a8-4068-b47b-31d727a06b7d (see BUG-13).

Preconditions

Steps
  1. 1. POST V1 Void for the booking. 2. Book a second booking and POST V2 Void. 3. Record HTTP status and body for each.
Expected Result
Neither response is the 2026-08-05 baseline (HTTP 409, ErrorCode=OperationNotSupported, Context 'TravelportNdc does not exists'). Void is routed to a TravelportNdc handler and returns a 2xx success or a mapped business error. If the 409 is still returned, the build under test lacks this feature - stop and block the suite.
Actual Result
Neither response is the 2026-08-05 / Round 1 baseline: V1 Void is no longer 409 OperationNotSupported ("TravelportNdc does not exists"). Both versions now route to a TravelportNdc handler and return 200 voided:true. The suite gate is open. This is the change that matters most between Round 1 and Round 2.

Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 and TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03 passed. Staging only. A V1 TravelportNdc booking ticketed today.
Steps
  1. 1. V1 Search -> FareConfirm -> Book (capture pnr, gdsPNR, bookingToken, tickets). 2. Immediately POST V1 Void. 3. Record HTTP status, duration and full response body.
Expected Result
HTTP 2xx with Void succeeded (voided=true and the voided ticket listed). Not an error envelope, no raw Travelport payload. Reference contract = SabreNdc Void observed 2026-10-22: {voided, voidedTickets[{ticketStatus, ticketNumber, carrierCode}]}, V2 also passengersVoidedAncillaries[] and emdTickets[]; SPEC §2.15 still marks the shape UNKNOWN, so record the TravelportNdc shape as its own baseline.
Actual Result
V1 Void succeeds for a same-day TravelportNdc booking: 200, voided=true, the ticket listed with ticketStatus Voided; no error envelope and no raw Travelport payload in the success body. Recorded V1 success contract: {voided, voidedTickets[{ticketStatus, ticketNumber, carrierCode}]}, exactly the SabreNdc V1 shape and without the V2-only fields. In Round 1 the same request returned 409 OperationNotSupported (fixed).

View Test Case
Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 passed with canBeHeld=true on the chosen offer (TravelportNdc Hold = Supported, confirmed live 2026-08-05).
Steps
  1. 1. Search -> FareConfirm -> (V2: AddPassenger ->) Hold -> FareConfirmAfterHold (PnrReprice) -> Retrieve -> BookAfterHold -> Retrieve. 2. Confirm tickets[] populated and record voidCapability. 3. POST Void the same day. 4. Record response.
Expected Result
HTTP 2xx with the same success shape as POS-01/02 (per version). pnr/gdsPNR/bookingToken unchanged since Hold (same-PNR invariant), and Void behaves identically for a booking that started as a Hold.
Actual Result
Both versions: Hold 200 with a holdExpirationDate, PnrReprice 200, BookAfterHold 200 issuing a ticket under the same pnr, gdsPNR and bookingToken (same-PNR invariant holds), and Void then succeeds exactly as for a direct Book. voidCapability is FullVoidOnlyAllowed on BookAfterHold and on the ticketed Retrieve but ABSENT on Hold, PnrReprice and the held Retrieve (logged under TC-VOIDTPN-BIZ-05). The void window is measured from BookAfterHold: ticketing was seconds after Hold in this run, so the two timestamps are not distinguishable in a same-session test.

Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 and TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03 passed. Staging only. Booking ticketed today with one ticket per passenger.
Steps
  1. 1. Book a 3-passenger TravelportNdc booking; record every ticket number. 2. POST Void with voidTickets=[]. 3. Retrieve the PNR.
Expected Result
Void succeeds; voidedTickets lists all 3 tickets (including the infant ticket); Retrieve shows every ticket in a voided state - none left active. Exact voided-state signal UNKNOWN (see TC-VOIDTPN-INT-02).
Actual Result
voidTickets=[] voids every ticket on the PNR: all 3 tickets (including the infant ticket) listed in voidedTickets on both versions, and Retrieve afterwards is the terminal 409 so no ticket is left active. Same as Round 1 on V2; V1 now behaves the same.

View Test Case
Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 and TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03 passed. Staging only. Multi-passenger booking ticketed today.
Steps
  1. 1. Book; collect all ticket numbers. 2. POST Void with voidTickets=[all ticket numbers]. 3. Retrieve.
Expected Result
Behaves identically to voidTickets=[] (all tickets voided). Record the accepted element shape of voidTickets (plain string vs object) - SPEC §2.15 marks it UNKNOWN.
Actual Result
Listing all 3 tickets behaves identically to [] (all 3 voided). Accepted element shape recorded: an OBJECT {ticketNumber, carrierCode, ticketStatus}; plain-string elements are rejected with a 400 (errorCode 1001) naming $.voidTickets[0] on both versions, not a 500.
☑️Validation7 passed3 failed
TC-VOIDTPN-VAL-01 - [Request] Validate missing or empty pnr is rejected before reaching TravelportNdc.PASS
Endpoint Name: Void without a booking reference
Request: Sent the void with the booking reference missing, then empty, on both versions
Response: Both versions refused it as invalid and the booking stayed ticketed
Expected: The void is refused with a clear message naming the missing field
Actual: Passed on both versions (a fix compared with Round 1)
Status: PASS
Evidence
Retrieve after each call: 200, ticket Booked (booking intact); one fresh booking per variant was created and voided at cleanup.

View Test Case
Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 and TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03 passed. Staging only. The booking has a real non-empty gdsPNR (e.g. H07WD3 style).
Steps
  1. 1. POST Void with gdsPNR=''. 2. If rejected, POST with gdsPNR omitted. 3. Retrieve the booking after each call.
Expected Result
Confirm live: either (a) rejected with 400 ValidationError naming gdsPNR (mandatory for GDS-routed TravelportNdc), or (b) Void succeeds because the integration resolves the record locator from pnr/bookingToken. A 500 or a generic Travelport fault is a defect. Record which.
Actual Result
Answer to the open SPEC 2.15 question, option (a): gdsPNR is MANDATORY for TravelportNdc on both versions. "" and omitted both give 400 NDC-INT-TEC-A0001 "GdsPnr is required"; the booking stays ticketed. No 500 and no raw Travelport fault. (SabreNdc accepted gdsPNR="".)

View Test Case
Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 and TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03 passed. Staging only. Same-day ticketed TravelportNdc booking (reuse one booking for the VAL cases only while Void keeps being rejected).
Steps
  1. 1. POST Void with a wrong surName. 2. POST Void without surName. 3. Retrieve the booking.
Expected Result
Wrong surName: rejected with a 4xx standard envelope, booking not voided (SPEC §2.15 Common Errors). Omitted surName: confirm live whether mandatory for TravelportNdc and record the result.
Actual Result
surName is not validated on either version. A surname that matches no passenger ("Mismatch") and a missing surName both return 200 voided:true and the ticket is voided (Retrieve 409). Expected a 4xx with the booking left ticketed. High: a caller that knows only a PNR can void a booking. Same defect as Round 1 on V2 and SabreNdc 2026-10-22; V1 now shows it too because V1 Void now works.
TC-VOIDTPN-VAL-05 - [Request] Validate missing supplier or credentialsSelector is rejected.PASS
Endpoint Name: Void without supplier or credentials
Request: Sent the void without the supplier, then without the credentials selector, on both versions
Response: Both were refused and the message names the missing field
Expected: A clear refusal naming the missing field and no booking changed
Actual: Passed on both versions
Status: PASS
Evidence
Retrieve after each call: 200, ticket Booked.

View Test Case
Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 and TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03 passed. Staging only. Same-day ticketed TravelportNdc booking (reuse one booking for the VAL cases only while Void keeps being rejected).
Steps
  1. 1. POST Void without supplier. 2. POST Void without credentialsSelector. 3. Retrieve the booking.
Expected Result
HTTP 400 ValidationError naming the missing field; no default supplier/selector silently applied; booking not voided.
Actual Result
Both versions: HTTP 400 {status, errorCode "1001", errorMessage "Validation errors occurred...", context [{name "Supplier", value "Select a valid Supplier"}]} and the same naming CredentialsSelector; no default supplier or selector is applied; booking not voided. Note this 400 uses the camelCase 1001 envelope while the pnr/bookingToken 400s use the PascalCase NDC-INT-TEC-A0001 envelope (see NEG-05).

Expected: Bad values are refused; leaving it out is recorded
Actual: Passed on both versions
Status: PASS

Omitted voidTickets: V1 ticket 1572141602442 and V2 ticket 1572141602440 voided (void-all).

View Test Case
Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 and TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03 passed. Staging only. Same-day ticketed TravelportNdc booking (reuse one booking for the VAL cases only while Void keeps being rejected).
Steps
  1. 1. POST Void once per variant. 2. Retrieve the booking after each call.
Expected Result
Wrong-type variants: HTTP 400 ValidationError naming voidTickets, not 500; booking not voided. Omitted/null voidTickets: confirm live whether treated as void-all or rejected, and record it.
Actual Result
String and [123]: 400 errorCode 1001 naming $.voidTickets / $.voidTickets[0], not a 500, booking intact. null: 400 "The VoidTickets field is required.", booking intact. Omitted: treated as void-all (both versions void the ticket), which is the answer to "omitted: confirm live". Observation: null is rejected while an omitted field voids everything, an inconsistent pair worth a decision. The type-name text in the 400 is logged under VAL-07.
TC-VOIDTPN-VAL-07 - [Response] Verify the Void response follows the integration contract and does not expose raw TravelportNdc payloads.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Check what the void response exposes
Request: Looked at the successful and failed void responses field by field
Response: Successful responses are clean; failed ones expose the supplier's raw reply and internal technical names
Expected: No raw supplier data and no internal names in any response
Actual: Failed: error responses leak raw supplier data and internal names
Status: FAIL
Evidence
Fields: OriginalSupplierRequest, OriginalSupplierResponse (409); context[].value with System.* / NDC.Integrations.* names (400).

View Test Case
Preconditions
TC-VOIDTPN-POS-01/02 executed.
Steps
  1. 1. Inspect success and failure response bodies field by field. 2. Look for Travelport-native structures (NDC JSON/XML fragments, Travelport error codes, supplierRequest/supplierResponse, credentials, PCC/branch codes, .NET DTO type names such as ...TravelportNdc...Dto).
Expected Result
Success: integration-defined fields only (shape recorded as baseline, same field names and types as the existing contract). Failure: standard envelope {Status, TransactionId, ErrorCode, ErrorMessage, Context}, Status equal to the HTTP code, TransactionId a GUID. No raw Travelport payload, no credentials, no DTO type names in Context.
Actual Result
The success contract is clean, but failures break the integration contract: the raw supplier request and response are echoed in the error body (409, both versions) and internal DTO type names plus parser positions are exposed in the 400 (both versions). No credentials or PCC values were seen in these Void bodies. Same defect as Round 1 (BUG-05); the 409 envelope field names are Status/TransactionId/ErrorCode/ErrorMessage/Context as documented, plus the two extra raw fields.

View Test Case
Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 and TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03 passed. Staging only. Same-day ticketed TravelportNdc booking (reuse one booking for the VAL cases only while Void keeps being rejected).
Steps
  1. 1. POST Void per variant. 2. Retrieve the booking after each call.
Expected Result
Whitespace-only and over-length: HTTP 400 ValidationError, never 500. Case variants: record whether the PNR lookup is case-insensitive; a lowercased real pnr voiding the booking is acceptable only if documented, otherwise note it.
Actual Result
pnr: whitespace-only is now a 400 ("PNR is required", fixed since Round 1) and 256 characters is a 400 ("Maximum length of a PNR is 9 characters"), both with the booking intact; the lower-cased real pnr is accepted and voids the booking (lookup is by gdsPNR so the pnr text is not compared, record as an undocumented behaviour). bookingToken: whitespace-only is a 400, but an upper-cased token and a 1000-character token are accepted and void the booking on both versions. Expected a 400 for the over-length token and a token match; the token is only checked for presence (BUG-03).
TC-VOIDTPN-BND-02 - [Request] Validate the calendar-day boundary: Void just before midnight is accepted and just after midnight is rejected.BLOCKED
Endpoint Name: Void just before and after midnight
Request: No request was sent
Response: Not run
Expected: Void accepted just before midnight, refused just after
Actual: Blocked: needs a midnight crossing
Status: BLOCKED
Evidence
Run exploratorily across midnight, or confirm the cut-off rule with the dev team first. BIZ-01 (aged ticket) is the alternative way to learn the boundary.

View Test Case
Preconditions
TC-VOIDTPN-POS-01 or POS-02 succeeded on this PNR.
Steps
  1. 1. POST the identical Void again. 2. POST a third time after 30 seconds. 3. Retrieve.
Expected Result
Second Void rejected with a 4xx standard envelope (already voided; exact code UNKNOWN - record); no 500; booking state unchanged; no duplicate voided entries.
Actual Result
A repeat Void is rejected on both versions with a 4xx standard envelope: 409 NDC-INT-BYP-A0003 "Reservation is already cancelled." (TERMINAL: RESERVATION IS CANCELLED AND CANNOT BE RETRIEVED (AIRLINE QR)); identical on the 30-second retry; no 500, no duplicate voided entries, state unchanged. Void is therefore NOT idempotent (it is not a 2xx no-op), the opposite of SabreNdc (BUG-04). The 409 body still carries the raw supplier payload (logged under VAL-07).

    "passengersCancelledAncillaries": null

View Test Case
Preconditions
Hold succeeded (tickets[] empty, holdExpirationDate set).
Steps
  1. 1. Search -> FareConfirm -> (V2: AddPassenger ->) Hold. 2. POST Void. 3. Retrieve. 4. Clean up with CancelAfterHold.
Expected Result
Void rejected as not eligible (no tickets) in the standard envelope; booking stays held. If Void cancels the hold instead, record it as a behavior to confirm with the team (CancelAfterHold is the documented path for holds, §2.14).
Actual Result
Void of a held booking is now rejected on both versions: 409 {ErrorCode NDC-INT-UNC-Z9999, Context BUSINESS_CONFLICT "This booking is on hold and not ticketed. Cancel it with the cancel hold flow instead of voiding it."}; the booking stays held (Retrieve 200, no tickets, holdExpirationDate unchanged; V2 bookingStatus OnHold) and CancelAfterHold remains the documented way out. Fixed since Round 1, when V2 returned 200 voided:false and silently cancelled the hold. Remaining flaw: the code is the unmapped Z9999 with ErrorMessage equal to the code (see NEG-05).

View Test Case
Preconditions
Those cases executed.
Steps
  1. 1. Compare voidCapability before each Void with the Void result. 2. Compare voidCapability after a successful Void.
Expected Result
Allowed value before same-day Void -> Void succeeded; VoidNotAllowed (or equivalent) on an aged ticket -> Void rejected; after a successful Void, voidCapability no longer reports void allowed. Any disagreement between flag and outcome is a defect. A field that is absent everywhere is itself a recurrence of the missing-voidCapability defect.
Actual Result
Improved since Round 1 (flag was absent everywhere): the flag is now present and consistent for ticketed bookings. It is still missing on every held-booking response, where a "void not allowed" value is exactly what a caller needs (SabreNdc returns VoidNotAllowed on Hold). The aged-ticket branch (VoidNotAllowed after the calendar day) could not be exercised because BIZ-01 is blocked. Failing on the held-booking omission (BUG-01, narrowed).
TC-VOIDTPN-BIZ-06 - [Response] Verify Void with voidTickets listing only a subset of the PNR's tickets voids exactly those tickets or is rejected.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Void only one ticket of three
Request: Asked to void just the adult ticket of a three-passenger booking, on both versions
Response: All three tickets were voided, including the infant
Expected: Either only the adult ticket is voided, or the request is refused
Actual: Failed: the whole booking was voided
Status: FAIL

View Test Case
Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 and TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03 passed. Staging only. 3-ticket booking ticketed today.
Steps
  1. 1. POST Void with voidTickets=[one ticket]. 2. Retrieve and compare each ticket's ticketStatus.
Expected Result
Either (a) only the listed ticket is voided and the others stay Booked, with voidedTickets listing exactly one entry, or (b) the request is rejected with a 4xx stating partial void is unsupported. Silently voiding all tickets, or voiding none while returning voided=true, is a defect.
Actual Result
The list is ignored on both versions: all 3 tickets (ADT, CHD and INF) are voided and returned, not the one that was asked for. Neither allowed outcome happened (voiding only the listed ticket, or rejecting a partial void). Same as Round 1 on V2 (BUG-09); V1 now shows it too.
TC-VOIDTPN-BIZ-07 - &[BookAfterHold] [Response] Verify CancelAfterHold and BookAfterHold on a voided TravelportNdc booking are rejected and Retrieve reports the voided state.PASS
Endpoint Name: Re-use a voided booking
Request: Tried to cancel the hold and to confirm the booking again after it was voided, on both versions
Response: Both were refused as already cancelled and nothing was re-issued
Expected: A voided booking cannot be re-ticketed
Actual: Passed on both versions
Status: PASS
Evidence
BookAfterHold on the voided PNR: 409 on V1 and V2.

View Test Case
Preconditions
Two ticketed TravelportNdc bookings today.
Steps
  1. 1. POST Void on A with variant (a). 2. Retrieve A. 3. POST Void on A with variant (b). 4. Retrieve A and B.
Expected Result
Both rejected with a 4xx standard envelope; A's and B's tickets unchanged. Must not silently void all of A's tickets, and must never void B's ticket.
Actual Result
Neither variant is rejected on either version. Both void ALL tickets of the booking named by the gdsPNR (Retrieve 409). Another booking's ticket was never voided (the foreign booking stayed ticketed), so the cross-booking harm did not occur, but a made-up or foreign ticket number silently becomes void-all. Same as Round 1 (BUG-09) and SabreNdc BUG-02.

View Test Case
Preconditions
A ticketed TravelportNdc (UAE) booking today. An inactive selector identified by TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-04.
Steps
  1. 1. POST Void with the inactive selector. 2. Retrieve with UAE.
Expected Result
4xx standard envelope with the 'credentials ... do not exist or are not active' message (or a cross-tenant rejection); booking not voided.
Actual Result
Both versions: 400 NDC-INT-TEC-A0001 with Context "The credentials for the selected supplier do not exist or are not active. Please verify the 'credentialsSelector' value."; booking not voided (Retrieve 200, ticket Booked).
TC-VOIDTPN-NEG-05 - [Response] Verify error responses for all failed Void scenarios use one consistent envelope.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Void error messages are consistent
Request: Compared the error format of every refused void
Response: Two different formats and a generic code are used for different problems
Expected: One consistent error format with distinct codes
Actual: Failed: two formats and an unclear generic code
Status: FAIL
Evidence
Envelope keys: Status/TransactionId/ErrorCode/ErrorMessage/Context vs status/transactionId/errorCode/errorMessage/context.

View Test Case
Preconditions
Those cases executed.
Steps
  1. 1. Tabulate HTTP status, Status, ErrorCode, ErrorMessage, Context per failure. 2. Compare.
Expected Result
Every failure uses {Status, TransactionId, ErrorCode, ErrorMessage, Context}; Status equals the HTTP code; validation errors are 400; business-rule/eligibility errors use one consistent code family. Record the full mapping table for SPEC.md §2.15.
Actual Result
Not one consistent envelope: the two validation 400s differ in key casing and code (NDC-INT-TEC-A0001 vs 1001); the business-rule family mixes BYP-A0003 and the unmapped Z9999, whose ErrorMessage is just the code, and the same Z9999 code covers four unrelated conditions (unknown PNR, held booking, wrong selector, cancelled EK booking). Same as Round 1 (BUG-11). Table to feed SPEC.md 2.15.
TC-VOIDTPN-NEG-06 - [Response] Verify the same invalid supplier or credentialsSelector gives the same error shape on Void as on Search and Book.PASS
Endpoint Name: Same error for an invalid supplier everywhere
Request: Sent an unknown supplier and selector to search, book and void on both versions
Response: All six were refused with the same message
Expected: The same refusal on every endpoint
Actual: Passed
Status: PASS
Evidence
Context also leaks the .NET enum type name (logged under VAL-07 / BUG-05 family).

View Test Case
Preconditions
A ticketed TravelportNdc (UAE) booking today. SabreNdc/EGY active.
Steps
  1. 1. POST Void variant (a). 2. POST Void variant (b). 3. Retrieve with TravelportNdc/UAE.
Expected Result
Both rejected (cross-tenant access denied or booking not found); booking still ticketed.
Actual Result
(a) 409 NDC-INT-UNC-Z9999 with Context 060004 "Order not found: orderId=[<the booking token>]" in ~1s on both versions: the SabreNdc handler looked the token up and found nothing, so a TravelportNdc PNR cannot be voided through the Sabre route. (b) 409 NDC-INT-UNC-Z9999 with an empty Context after ~9-10s on both versions: the call is forwarded to Travelport under the EGY credentials and refused there. Both refused, both bookings still ticketed. Remaining flaws are the unmapped Z9999 code and the empty context in (b) (see NEG-05). Variant (a) only addresses the SabreNdc void route with a throwaway TravelportNdc booking; no SabreNdc booking is involved.
TC-VOIDTPN-SEC-04 - [Request] Validate injection payloads in surName and pnr are rejected or safely handled.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Void with injection text in the name and booking reference
Request: Put database and script text, and a very long text, into the surname and the booking reference, on both versions
Response: The booking reference was refused; the surname was accepted and the booking voided
Expected: Every odd value is refused and no booking is voided
Actual: Failed: the surname is not validated
Status: FAIL
Evidence
V1: tickets 1572141602464 / 1572141602467 / 1572141602469 voided; V2: 1572141602461 / 1572141602491 / 1572141602494 voided.

View Test Case
Preconditions
Void succeeded.
Steps
  1. 1. POST Retrieve (V1 RetrieveBooking / V2 Retrieve) immediately after Void. 2. Record status, tickets[].ticketStatus, voidCapability, and any status field.
Expected Result
Booking shows as voided: tickets[].ticketStatus changed from Booked to a voided value and voidCapability no longer allows void - or a terminal 409 like cancelled PNRs. Exact signal UNKNOWN (bookingStatus does not exist in V1 Retrieve, §2.11, confirmed on TravelportNdc 2026-08-05) - record it as the baseline. Unchanged Booked tickets = defect.
Actual Result
After a successful Void Retrieve fails on both versions with the terminal 409 used for cancelled PNRs: Qatar Airways bookings give NDC-INT-BYP-A0003 "Reservation is already cancelled." and Emirates bookings give NDC-INT-UNC-Z9999 with Context ReservationCancelled "Reservation is already cancelled". There is no voided bookingStatus or ticketStatus to read back (V1 Retrieve has no bookingStatus at all; V2 bookingStatus was Booked before the Void), so a voided booking and a cancelled hold look identical and the voidCapability flag cannot be re-read. This resolves the SPEC 6.3 vs 2.11 contradiction. The 409 body also carries the raw supplier payload (VAL-07).

Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 passed.
Steps
  1. 1. Search -> FareConfirm -> Hold -> Retrieve -> CancelAfterHold -> Retrieve. 2. Search -> FareConfirm -> Book -> Retrieve. 3. Compare with the 2026-08-05 baseline.
Expected Result
Hold returns a holdExpirationDate; CancelAfterHold returns {cancelled:true, message:'Reservation cancelled successfully.'} and a follow-up Retrieve returns 409 NDC-INT-BYP-A0003 'Reservation is already cancelled'; Book returns 200 with synchronously issued tickets and Retrieve echoes them.
Actual Result
Unchanged from the baseline on both versions: Hold returns a holdExpirationDate (2026-11-02 21:59); CancelAfterHold returns {cancelled:true, message:"Reservation cancelled successfully."} (V2 adds passengersCancelledAncillaries: null); the follow-up Retrieve is 409 NDC-INT-BYP-A0003 "Reservation is already cancelled."; Book is 200 with synchronously issued tickets and Retrieve echoes them. The only change from 2026-08-05 is the additive voidCapability on ticketed Book/Retrieve.

Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 and TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03 passed. Staging only. Collection variables cleared (§6.1). Whole flow run without delay on one calendar day.
Steps
  1. Search (capture searchResponseId, offerId) -> FareConfirm (capture fareConfirmResponseId, selectedOfferId; price reconciliation) -> Book (passengersList, contactsList; capture pnr, gdsPNR, bookingToken, tickets, voidCapability) -> Retrieve (tickets[].ticketStatus=Booked) -> Void (supplier, credentialsSelector, pnr, gdsPNR, bookingToken, surName, voidTickets=[]) -> Retrieve (post-Void check)
Expected Result
Every hop HTTP 200/2xx; Void succeeds; final Retrieve shows all tickets voided (signal per TC-VOIDTPN-INT-02). Price reconciliation holds through Book.
Actual Result
Every hop passes and the price reconciles through Book (1815 AED at Search, FareConfirm and Book). Void succeeds on V1 and the final Retrieve is the terminal 409 "Reservation is already cancelled" (signal per INT-02). In Round 1 and on 2026-08-05 this flow failed at the Void hop with 409 OperationNotSupported; that is fixed.

Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 and TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03 passed. Staging only. canBeHeld=true on the chosen offer. Collection variables cleared. Run on one calendar day.
Steps
  1. Search -> FareConfirm -> Hold (capture pnr, gdsPNR, bookingToken, holdExpirationDate) -> FareConfirmAfterHold (PnrReprice) -> Retrieve -> BookAfterHold (IDs unchanged; tickets populated) -> Retrieve -> Void -> Retrieve (post-Void check)
Expected Result
All hops succeed before holdExpirationDate; BookAfterHold issues tickets; Void succeeds; final Retrieve shows all tickets voided.
Actual Result
Family-E chain works end to end on V1: the hold is repriced (1815 AED unchanged), ticketed from the hold with pnr, gdsPNR and bookingToken unchanged, then voided; the final Retrieve is the terminal 409. Round 1 failed at the Void hop.

View Test Case
Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 and TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03 passed. Staging only. Collection variables cleared. Run on one calendar day.
Steps
  1. Search -> UpSelling (capture upSellingResponseId and the selected tier's offerId) -> Book (using the upselling ids) -> Retrieve -> Void -> Retrieve (post-Void check)
Expected Result
Every hop succeeds; the booked tier's price matches the Upselling tier; Void succeeds; final Retrieve shows all tickets voided.
Actual Result
The booked fare equals the Upselling tier (1815 AED), Void succeeds and the final Retrieve is the terminal 409. The flow still fails on one hop: V1 Upselling returns upsellOffers[] and no selectedOffer, so the documented drop-in for FareConfirm does not hold and the first tier had to be chosen by hand. Void is no longer the failing step (it was in Round 1).
FLOW-V1-11-TPN - [Search]&[UpSelling]&[Hold]&[BookAfterHold]&[Void] [Response] Verify Family-E flow #11 completes end to end for TravelportNdc.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Whole V1 upsell-and-hold flow ending in a void
Request: Upsold, held, ticketed from the hold, voided and checked on version 1
Response: Everything worked except that the upsell step does not return the chosen offer as documented
Expected: Every step works and the final lookup shows the ticket voided
Actual: Failed on the upsell step
Status: FAIL
Evidence
ok Search offer reconciles (fully itemized offer picked) (28 of 53 offers fully itemized); FAIL Upselling returns selectedOffer (documented drop-in for FareConfirm) (keys: responseId,supplier,journeys,flightSegments,priceClasses,baggageDetails,upsellOffers); ok Upselling tier reconciles; ok Hold selectedOffer reconciles; ok Hold total equals Upselling tier total (1815 vs 1815); ok FareConfirmAfterHold (PnrReprice) 200; ok BookAfterHold issues tickets; ids unchanged (pnr PY6J86 token same true); ok Retrieve before Void shows tickets Booked (1765766802355:Booked); ok Void succeeds (2xx, voided=true) (200 200 {"voided":true,"voidedTickets":[{"ticketStatus":"Voided","ticketNumber":"1765766802355","carrierCode":"EK"}]})

Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 and TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03 passed. Staging only. canBeHeld=true on the chosen upselling tier. Run on one calendar day.
Steps
  1. Search -> UpSelling -> Hold -> FareConfirmAfterHold (PnrReprice) -> Retrieve -> BookAfterHold -> Retrieve -> Void -> Retrieve (post-Void check)
Expected Result
All hops succeed before holdExpirationDate; Void succeeds; final Retrieve shows all tickets voided; IDs unchanged from Hold.
Actual Result
Hold, reprice, ticketing from the hold (ids unchanged), Void and the final Retrieve all work. The flow fails only because V1 Upselling returns upsellOffers[] and no selectedOffer (same defect as FLOW-V1-09-TPN). Round 1 failed at the Void hop.

Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 and TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03 passed. Staging only. Collection variables cleared. Run on one calendar day.
Steps
  1. Search -> FareConfirm -> AddPassenger (capture getAddPaxResponceID, getAddPaxOfferId) -> Book (ResponseId, selectedOfferId; capture pnr, gdsPNR, bookingToken, tickets, voidCapability) -> Retrieve -> Void (real gdsPNR, not the saved example's '') -> Retrieve (post-Void check)
Expected Result
Every hop succeeds; Void succeeds; final Retrieve shows all tickets voided.
Actual Result
Every hop succeeds, the price reconciles through Book (1815 AED), Void succeeds and the final Retrieve is the terminal 409. The minimal V2 Book body that works is {supplier, credentialsSelector, ResponseId = AddPassenger responseId, selectedOfferId = AddPassenger offerId}. Same as Round 1.

Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 and TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03 passed. Staging only. canBeHeld=true on the chosen offer. Collection variables cleared. Run on one calendar day.
Steps
  1. Search -> FareConfirm -> AddPassenger -> Hold -> FareConfirmAfterHold -> Retrieve -> BookAfterHold -> Retrieve -> Void -> Retrieve (post-Void check)
Expected Result
All hops succeed before holdExpirationDate; Void succeeds; final Retrieve shows all tickets voided.
Actual Result
All hops succeed before holdExpirationDate, BookAfterHold issues the ticket under unchanged ids, Void succeeds and the final Retrieve is the terminal 409. V2 Retrieve shows bookingStatus OnHold then Booked. Same as Round 1.

Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 and TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03 passed. Staging only. Collection variables cleared. Run on one calendar day.
Steps
  1. Search -> UpSelling -> AddPassenger -> Book -> Retrieve -> Void -> Retrieve (post-Void check)
Expected Result
Every hop succeeds with AddPassenger inserted; Void succeeds; final Retrieve shows all tickets voided.
Actual Result
Every hop succeeds with AddPassenger inserted, the booked tier price equals the Upselling tier (1815 AED), Void succeeds and the final Retrieve is the terminal 409. Anomaly question answered again: Book does NOT work without AddPassenger (HTTP 500 instead of a 400 naming the missing passenger details), so AddPassenger is required for flows 72-89 (BUG-12, 2nd confirmation). The V2 Upselling "selectedOffer" check below is informational: V2 Upselling returns upsellOffers[] by design.
FLOW-V2-76-TPN - [Search]&[UpSelling]&[AddPassenger]&[Hold]&[BookAfterHold]&[Void] [Response] Verify Family-E flow #76 completes end to end for TravelportNdc.PASS
Endpoint Name: Whole V2 upsell-and-hold flow ending in a void
Request: Upsold, added passenger details, held, ticketed from the hold, voided and checked on version 2; needed three tries because the airline had two temporary errors
Response: The third try worked end to end; the two earlier tries hit temporary airline errors
Expected: Every step works and the final lookup shows the ticket voided
Actual: Passed on the third attempt after two temporary airline errors
Status: PASS

View Test Case
Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 and TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03 passed. Staging only. canBeHeld=true on the chosen upselling tier. Run on one calendar day.
Steps
  1. Search -> UpSelling -> AddPassenger -> Hold -> FareConfirmAfterHold -> Retrieve -> BookAfterHold -> Retrieve -> Void -> Retrieve (post-Void check)
Expected Result
All hops succeed before holdExpirationDate; Void succeeds; final Retrieve shows all tickets voided.
Actual Result
On a clean attempt the Family-E chain works end to end, the tier price (1985 AED) is unchanged through Hold, ids stay the same after BookAfterHold, Void succeeds and the final Retrieve is the terminal 409. Two earlier attempts the same hour failed on transient Emirates-side errors (reservation update in progress at Void; no response from vendor at ticketing). They are supplier conditions, not logic errors, so the verdict follows the clean attempt, but the API handling of them is poor: a retryable TEMPORARY error is returned as the unmapped 409 Z9999 with ErrorMessage equal to the code, the raw supplier payload and no retry indication (BUG-14). The flow therefore needed one retry of the Void to complete in attempt 1.
FLOW-V1-03-TPN-NEGHOP5 - [Search]&[FareConfirm]&[Book]&[Retrieve]&[Void] [Request] Validate Family-C flow #3 rejects a stale bookingToken at the Void hop for TravelportNdc.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Void a flow booking using another booking's token (version 1)
Request: Ran the booking flow and swapped in a different booking's token at the void step
Response: The void was accepted and the booking voided
Expected: The void is refused and the booking stays ticketed
Actual: Failed: the foreign token is accepted
Status: FAIL
Evidence
ok Search offer reconciles (fully itemized offer picked) (28 of 53 offers fully itemized); ok FareConfirm reconciles; ok FareConfirm total equals Search total (1815 vs 1815); ok Book selectedOffer reconciles; ok Book total equals FareConfirm tier total (1815 vs 1815); ok Retrieve before Void shows tickets Booked (1765766802359:Booked); Void accepted the foreign token (voided=true)

View Test Case
Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 and TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03 passed. Staging only. A second ticketed TravelportNdc booking exists to supply the foreign token.
Steps
  1. Run FLOW-V1-03-TPN through hop 4 (Retrieve). At hop 5 replace bookingToken with the one from another booking. Retrieve both bookings afterwards.
Expected Result
Void rejected with a 4xx standard envelope; the flow's booking stays ticketed.
Actual Result
The stale / foreign bookingToken is not rejected: the flow's own booking is voided with another booking's token. Expected a 4xx and the booking left ticketed. Round 1 could not run this on V1 (Void unsupported); it fails now for the same reason as NEG-02 (BUG-03).
FLOW-V2-27-TPN-NEGHOP6 - [Search]&[FareConfirm]&[AddPassenger]&[Book]&[Retrieve]&[Void] [Request] Validate Family-C flow #27 rejects a stale bookingToken at the Void hop for TravelportNdc.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Void a flow booking using another booking's token (version 2)
Request: Ran the booking flow and swapped in a different booking's token at the void step
Response: The void was accepted and the booking voided
Expected: The void is refused and the booking stays ticketed
Actual: Failed: the foreign token is accepted

View Test Case
Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 and TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03 passed. Staging only. A second ticketed TravelportNdc booking exists to supply the foreign token.
Steps
  1. Run FLOW-V2-27-TPN through hop 5 (Retrieve). At hop 6 replace bookingToken with the one from another booking. Retrieve both bookings afterwards.
Expected Result
Void rejected with a 4xx standard envelope; the flow's booking stays ticketed.
Actual Result
The stale / foreign bookingToken is not rejected: the flow's own booking is voided with another booking's token. Expected a 4xx and the booking left ticketed. Same as Round 1 (BUG-03).
Findings12Defects8Unknown-resolution
Defect — BUG-13, 1st confirmed occurrence (not new)
Two different TravelportNdc bookings can be returned the same bookingToken: V1 774MNY and V2 773JKY (made in the same second) both got 96e14dee-43a8-4068-b47b-31d727a06b7d; V1 774VYF and 774AIE both got e68b0a9f-ed6b-4d3a-b5b1-4d81684e795e (§2.9 voidCapability; §2.11; §4.7, TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-02)
Field: bookingToken
Expected value: A bookingToken that is unique per booking, e.g. a fresh GUID for every Book/Hold response
History: New in Round 2: not seen in Round 1 (Round 1 bookings were created sequentially).
Impact: bookingToken is the third id every downstream call (Retrieve, Void, BookAfterHold, CancelAfterHold) is meant to bind to the booking; if two bookings share it, it cannot identify or authorise either one, and any future token check (BUG-03) would let one booking's holder act on the other See full bug report.
Evidence: 2 shared-token pairs among 102 bookings created in this round; the pairs were created concurrently (same ticketing second 2026-10-27T06:15:23 for the first pair). Different pnr and gdsPNR in each pair (774MNY/HNGKWD vs 773JKY/HNGKWF).
Defect — BUG-04, 2nd confirmed occurrence (not new)
TravelportNdc Void ignores surName on V1 and V2: a surname that matches no passenger, or no surname at all, voids the booking (200 voided:true) (§2.15 Common Errors; AC Business Rules, TC-VOIDTPN-VAL-04)
Field: surName
Expected value: 400/409 standard envelope, e.g. Context "surName does not match any passenger on the PNR", booking left ticketed
History: First observed Round 1 (2026-10-26, 20261026-105925_TravelportNdc-Void-UAE-V1V2); first seen on SabreNdc 2026-10-22 (BUG-01 there); in Round 2 it now also reproduces on V1 because V1 Void works
Impact: Anyone holding a PNR/gdsPNR can void a ticket without knowing the passenger surname; the ownership check the AC and SPEC 2.15 describe does not exist See full bug report.
Evidence: V1 ticket 1572141602475 and V2 ticket 1572141602427 voided with surName "Mismatch"; V1 1572141602474 and V2 1572141602426 voided with surName omitted
Defect — BUG-05, 2nd confirmed occurrence (not new)
TravelportNdc Void failures expose internal and supplier data: 409 bodies carry OriginalSupplierRequest and the raw Travelport OriginalSupplierResponse, and the 400 for a wrong-typed voidTickets quotes .NET type names (System.Collections.Generic.ICollection`1[NDC.Integrations.Application.Dtos.Api.SharedTypes.TicketType]) with parser positions (AC Result Mapping; AC Error Handling; §2.9 Expected Failure (DTO leak defect); §7.14, TC-VOIDTPN-VAL-07)
Field: Context[].Value / OriginalSupplierRequest / OriginalSupplierResponse
Expected value: {Status, TransactionId, ErrorCode, ErrorMessage, Context[{Name, Value}]} with integration-defined text only, no raw supplier payload and no type names
History: First observed Round 1 (2026-10-26, 20261026-105925_TravelportNdc-Void-UAE-V1V2); also seen on SabreNdc Void 2026-10-22; Round 2 reproduces on V1 and V2
Impact: Leaks supplier request/response structure and internal DTO names to every API consumer, and breaks the contract that supplier details are mapped See full bug report.
Evidence: Repeat Void (409 BYP-A0003) and unknown-PNR Void (409 Z9999) both carry OriginalSupplierRequest/Response on V1 and V2; VAL06-string V1 and VAL06-num V2 show the type names
Defect — BUG-06, 2nd confirmed occurrence (not new)
V2 Void returns passengersVoidedAncillaries: null for a booking without ancillaries (emdTickets is {}); SabreNdc returns {} (§2.15; §6.4 ANC, TC-VOIDTPN-VAL-10)
Field: passengersVoidedAncillaries
Expected value: "passengersVoidedAncillaries": {}
History: First observed Round 1 (2026-10-26, 20261026-105925_TravelportNdc-Void-UAE-V1V2); Round 2 reproduces it unchanged on V2
Impact: Consumers must null-check one field that is documented as a collection; V2 CancelAfterHold has the same null in passengersCancelledAncillaries See full bug report.
Evidence: V2 Void 773JKY: {"voided":true,"voidedTickets":[...],"passengersVoidedAncillaries":null,"emdTickets":{}}
Defect — BUG-03, 2nd confirmed occurrence (not new)
TravelportNdc Void only checks that bookingToken is non-empty: an upper-cased token, a 1000-character token and another booking's token all void the booking on V1 and V2 (§2.15; §8 string-field boundary angle, TC-VOIDTPN-BND-01)
Field: bookingToken
Expected value: 400 for an over-length token and a 4xx when the token does not belong to the PNR
History: First observed Round 1 (2026-10-26, 20261026-105925_TravelportNdc-Void-UAE-V1V2); Round 2 narrows it: an omitted, empty or whitespace-only bookingToken and a whitespace-only pnr are now rejected (400), but the token is still not matched to the booking
Impact: The token gives no protection: a caller with only a pnr/gdsPNR can void any booking by sending any non-blank string See full bug report.
Evidence: BND01-tok-1000 voided V1 1572141602452 and V2 1572141602487; BND01-tok-upper voided V1 1572141602478 and V2 1572141602447; NEG-02 mixed token voided V1 1572141602453 and V2 1572141602488
Defect — BUG-01, 2nd confirmed occurrence (not new)
voidCapability is missing on Hold, PnrReprice and Retrieve of a held booking on V1 and V2, so a held booking (Void refused) carries no "void not allowed" value (§2.9 voidCapability; §3.2; AC Business Rules, TC-VOIDTPN-BIZ-05)
Field: voidCapability
Expected value: "voidCapability": "VoidNotAllowed" on a held booking (SabreNdc Hold returns it) and on a ticket past the void window
History: First observed Round 1 (2026-10-26, 20261026-105925_TravelportNdc-Void-UAE-V1V2); absent on TravelportNdc V1 Book 2026-08-05 and on SabreNdc 2026-10-22/25; Round 2: Book, BookAfterHold and the ticketed Retrieve now return FullVoidOnlyAllowed (fixed), but Hold, PnrReprice and the held Retrieve still omit it
Impact: Callers cannot use the flag to decide whether to offer Void for a held booking; flag-vs-outcome consistency can only be shown for ticketed bookings See full bug report.
Evidence: h1_V1 775WP7 and h1_V2 775RZB: Hold, PnrReprice, Retrieve(after-hold) have no voidCapability key; BookAfterHold and Retrieve(after-BAH) return FullVoidOnlyAllowed
Defect — BUG-09, 2nd confirmed occurrence (not new)
TravelportNdc Void ignores the voidTickets list: asking for one ticket of a 3-ticket PNR voids all three, including the infant (§2.15 voidTickets; AC Business Rules, TC-VOIDTPN-BIZ-06)
Field: voidTickets
Expected value: Only the listed ticket voided, or a 4xx stating partial void is unsupported
History: First observed Round 1 (2026-10-26, 20261026-105925_TravelportNdc-Void-UAE-V1V2); Round 2 reproduces it on V2 and now on V1
Impact: A caller cannot void selectively and an infant ticket can be voided with no ADT linkage check; the list is also ignored for fabricated and foreign ticket numbers (NEG-03) See full bug report.
Evidence: V1 7746DZ and V2 773AYB: voidTickets [1 ticket] -> voidedTickets 3 tickets, Retrieve 409
Defect — BUG-10, 2nd confirmed occurrence (not new)
Void for an unknown record locator returns the unmapped 409 NDC-INT-UNC-Z9999 whose ErrorMessage repeats the code, plus the raw Travelport request and response (AC Error Handling; §2.15; §7.9, TC-VOIDTPN-NEG-01)
Field: ErrorCode / ErrorMessage
Expected value: 4xx with a meaningful code and message, e.g. 404/409 "Booking not found", and no raw supplier payload
History: First observed Round 1 (2026-10-26, 20261026-105925_TravelportNdc-Void-UAE-V1V2); Round 2 reproduces it on V1 and V2; also SabreNdc 2026-10-22
Impact: Consumers cannot tell "booking not found" from other Z9999 conditions (held booking, wrong selector, cancelled EK booking) and see supplier internals See full bug report.
Evidence: ZZZZZZ: {Status 409, ErrorCode NDC-INT-UNC-Z9999, ErrorMessage NDC-INT-UNC-Z9999, Context [VALIDATION "RECORD LOCATOR DOES NOT EXIST"], OriginalSupplierRequest "ZZZZZZ", OriginalSupplierResponse <raw>}
Defect — BUG-11, 2nd confirmed occurrence (not new)
Void errors use two envelope casings (PascalCase NDC-INT-TEC-A0001 vs camelCase errorCode "1001") and one generic NDC-INT-UNC-Z9999 whose ErrorMessage equals the code for four unrelated conditions (AC Error Handling; AC Result Mapping; §2.9 Expected Failure, TC-VOIDTPN-NEG-05)
Field: error envelope (ErrorCode / ErrorMessage)
Expected value: One envelope {Status, TransactionId, ErrorCode, ErrorMessage, Context} with distinct codes per condition
History: First observed Round 1 (2026-10-26, 20261026-105925_TravelportNdc-Void-UAE-V1V2); Round 2 reproduces it unchanged; SabreNdc Void had the same (BUG-07 2026-10-22)
Impact: Clients need two parsers and cannot branch on ErrorCode for held, unknown, wrong-selector and cancelled cases See full bug report.
Evidence: pnr/bookingToken/gdsPNR required -> NDC-INT-TEC-A0001; supplier/selector missing, wrong voidTickets type, pnr > 9 -> 1001; held booking, unknown pnr, other selector, cancelled EK booking -> Z9999
Defect — BUG-12, 2nd confirmed occurrence (not new)
V2 Book called with the Upselling ResponseId/offerId and no AddPassenger step returns HTTP 500 ServerError (§5.4 #74; §5.5 items 4-5; §6.3 Family C; §2.15, FLOW-V2-74-TPN)
Field: Book (V2) without AddPassenger
Expected value: 400 ValidationError naming the missing passenger details
History: First observed Round 1 (2026-10-26, 20261026-105925_TravelportNdc-Void-UAE-V1V2); Round 2 reproduces it on V2
Impact: A flow that skips AddPassenger (flow.md 72-89 omits it) fails with an opaque 500 instead of a usable validation error See full bug report.
Evidence: Book without AddPassenger: 500 {Status 500, ErrorCode ServerError, ErrorMessage "Unknown error occured...", Context []} in 1.0s, TransactionId 66e6198a-2027-416c-a004-619929c89236
Defect — BUG-14, 1st confirmed occurrence (not new)
Transient Emirates errors are returned as the unmapped 409 NDC-INT-UNC-Z9999 with the raw supplier response and no retry signal: Void "RESERVATION UPDATE IN PROGRESS. RETRY RESERVATION RETRIEVE" and BookAfterHold "DOCUMENT ISSUANCE FAILED. NO RESPONSE RECEIVED FROM VENDOR" (§5.4 #76; §5.5 items 4-5; §6.3 Family E; §2.15, FLOW-V2-76-TPN)
Field: ErrorCode / Context (TEMPORARY supplier error)
Expected value: A mapped retryable error (for example 503/409 with a RETRY code) and no raw payload; for Void the same request succeeds on resend (it did)
History: New in Round 2: two transient Emirates-side errors were returned in one hour as unmapped 409 Z9999 (Round 1 did not hit them).
Impact: Callers cannot distinguish a safe retry from a business refusal; a retry succeeded for the Void, while the failed BookAfterHold left a live hold that had to be cancelled See full bug report.
Evidence: Void TransactionId ed81a7bb-64de-4f1e-8648-8d699fa3b6cb (pnr FGJ5BB, retried OK); BookAfterHold TransactionId 7a3e7555-ea44-43ef-8208-ed5a4eb15bf8 (pnr BNRUZT, hold cancelled)
Defect — BUG-15, 3rd confirmed occurrence (not new)
V1 Upselling on TravelportNdc returns upsellOffers[] and no selectedOffer, so it is not the documented drop-in for FareConfirm (§5.4 #9; §2.3; §6.3 Family C; §2.15, FLOW-V1-09-TPN)
Field: selectedOffer (V1 Upselling)

BUG-02 (V1 Void returns 409 OperationNotSupported for TravelportNdc) — exercised by TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03, TC-VOIDTPN-POS-01, TC-VOIDTPN-REG-02, FLOW-V1-03-TPN, FLOW-V1-05-TPN, FLOW-V1-09-TPN, FLOW-V1-11-TPN. Exercised on all 80 V1 Void sends for TravelportNdc this round (bookings, flows and variants): all returned the Void handler's real answers (200 voided:true or the 400/409 validations). Never the OperationNotSupported 409. Looks fixed on the ne-5 build; recommend the dev team confirm and close.

BUG-07 (Whitespace-only pnr accepted by V2 Void) — exercised by TC-VOIDTPN-BND-01. A whitespace-only pnr is now a 400 "PNR is required" on V1 and V2 and the booking stays ticketed. Looks fixed; the lower-cased pnr is still accepted, which is harmless because the booking is located by gdsPNR.

BUG-08 (Void on a held booking returns 200 voided:false and cancels the hold) — exercised by TC-VOIDTPN-BIZ-03. Void on a held booking is now rejected with 409 BUSINESS_CONFLICT and the hold survives on V1 and V2 (CancelAfterHold remains the path). Looks fixed.

§2.15 Expected Success Response — status: pending

Old: "**Expected Success Response**: `UNKNOWN` for a void-eligible booking — not observed this run. `[Confirmed live 2026-08-05, V1/TravelportNdc]`: Void is **not supported** for this supplier at all"

New: "**Expected Success Response** `[Confirmed live 2026-10-27, TravelportNdc/UAE, V1 and V2, build ndc-integration-stg-ne-5]`: HTTP 200 `{voided: true, voidedTickets: [{ticketStatus: "Voided", ticketNumber, carrierCode}]}` on V1; V2 adds `passengersVoidedAncillaries: null` (defect: should be `{}`) and `emdTickets: {}`; 11-18s. Book ticketing is synchronous (~22-26s), so a same-day Void can follow at once; Void also works for a Hold > BookAfterHold booking. A held, unticketed booking is rejected (409 BUSINESS_CONFLICT), not voided. The 2026-08-05 / 2026-10-26 finding that V1 Void is unsupported for TravelportNdc no longer applies"

Correction: Supersedes the pending Round 1 proposal: V1 Void now works. From POS-01/02/03/04/05, BIZ-03 and the flows.

§2.15 Required Request Fields (voidTickets, gdsPNR) — status: pending

Old: "`voidTickets` (array, empty `[]` in every saved example — `UNKNOWN` exact shape when populated, presumably ticket numbers to selectively void vs. void-all-when-empty)."

New: "`voidTickets` `[Confirmed live 2026-10-27, TravelportNdc V1 and V2]`: array of `{ticketNumber, carrierCode, ticketStatus}` objects (plain strings and numbers: 400 errorCode 1001); `[]` and an omitted field void every ticket on the PNR, `null` is rejected. DEFECT: the list is not honoured (a subset, a fabricated number and another booking's ticket all void every ticket). `pnr` (max 9 characters), `bookingToken` and `gdsPNR` are mandatory (400 NDC-INT-TEC-A0001 "... is required" when omitted, empty or whitespace). The booking is located by `gdsPNR`; `bookingToken` is only checked for presence (an upper-cased, 1000-character or another booking's token still voids) and `surName` is not validated at all (DEFECTS)"
